beats.beat: The company operates in two segments: creation of infrastructure and operating a ready-mix concrete (RMC) plant. Its infrastructure work covers railways (platforms, station buildings, gauge conversion, track laying), bridges (beam, cantilever, arch, suspension, cable-stayed, truss), and roadways (bituminous and concrete roads).

Contracts are won through a competitive bidding process. The client floats a tender, a pre-bid meeting resolves queries, the contractor bids, and the job is awarded to the lowest quote. The contractor then deposits a performance guarantee and starts execution.

Major clients are government and public-sector entities: Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai, Western Railway, Central Railway, Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation Ltd, Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority, Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Ltd, and several private companies.
Revenue is heavily concentrated: the top customers contributed 57% of total revenue in fiscal 2018. Western Railway alone makes up 52% of the company's order book.
The order book is strong but contracts can be adjusted, cancelled or suspended by clients, meaning the order book is not necessarily indicative of future revenues.

beats.beat: Revenue from operations has declined: ₹90.21 crore in FY2015 to ₹60.53 crore in FY2018. The corresponding figure for FY2014 was ₹86.61 crore.
Net profit after adjustments was volatile: ₹0.96 crore (FY2014), ₹0.78 crore (FY2015), ₹0.33 crore (FY2016), ₹0.16 crore (FY2017), and ₹3.15 crore (FY2018). The sharp jump in FY2018 is notable.
EBITDA (Profit Before Interest, Depreciation and Tax) ranged between ₹6.76 crore (FY2017) and ₹9.46 crore (FY2015). FY2018 EBITDA was ₹9.29 crore.
Short-term borrowings rose from ₹30.82 crore in FY2014 to ₹35.37 crore in FY2018. Long-term borrowings stood at ₹1.33 crore as of FY2018. Total assets were ₹82.32 crore as of FY2018.
The company has experienced negative cash flows in recent financial years, which the filing warns could impact business and financial condition.

Key ratios as per the filing: EPS for FY2018 was ₹12.59, NAV per share ₹28.14, and RoNW 12.39%. For the three years shown, EPS was 1.31 (FY2016), 0.63 (FY2017), 12.59 (FY2018); RoNW was 44.71%, 12.39%, 12.39% respectively.

beats.beat: The promoter and managing director is Amit Bholanath Mishra, who holds 74,95,476 equity shares (90.949% of pre-issue capital). Other directors hold only 300 shares each.
Key management personnel: Ms. Anchal Pachori (CFO, aged 28, Chartered Accountant) and Mr. Mohit Soni (Company Secretary and Compliance Officer, aged 26, Associate Member of ICSI).

Related-party transactions in FY2018 include loans taken from KMP/Board of Directors of ₹68.4 lakhs, director remuneration of ₹57.7 lakhs, and outstanding payables to related parties of ₹324.3 lakhs as on 31 March 2018.

Two companies promoted by Amit Bholanath Mishra — Al-Noor Chickens Private Limited and A B Magma Automobiles Private Limited — were struck off by the Registrar of Companies in March 2016 due to non-operation of business.

The company has issued equity shares in the last 12 months at a price that may be lower than the IPO price. There is pending litigation involving the company, promoter and directors, but no specific details are provided in the excerpts.

beats.beat: The infrastructure sector, including power, bridges, dams, roads and urban development, contributes roughly 8% to India's GDP (at constant prices).

Key demand drivers include government flagship programmes such as 100 Smart Cities Mission, AMRUT, Make in India, and Power for All; eased FDI norms in 15 sectors including construction; and rising industrialisation, urbanisation, and disposable income.

India needs an estimated ₹50 trillion (US$ 777.73 billion) in infrastructure investment by 2022 for sustainable development. The logistics sector (related to construction) is expected to grow at a CAGR of 10.5% from US$ 160 billion in 2017 to US$ 215 billion by 2020.

The construction market is highly fragmented and competitive, with both organised and unorganised players. The company acknowledges slow government projects, working capital crunches, and policy changes as headwinds.

beats.beat: A B Infrabuild Limited is a Mumbai-based infrastructure and construction company that builds railway platforms, bridges, roads, and also operates a ready-mix concrete plant. It has worked for government clients like Western Railways, Central Railways, and the Mumbai civic body for over a decade. The company is raising funds through an SME IPO of 44.28 lakh fresh equity shares, primarily to meet working capital needs.
The issue is managed by Mark Corporate Advisors Private Limited and the price will be determined later.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: who A B Infrabuild is, its core business, and that it is launching an SME IPO to raise working capital.

beats.beat: The IPO consists of a fresh issue of 44,28,000 equity shares of ₹10 each at a price to be determined. There is no offer-for-sale component.
Proceeds will be used to meet working capital requirements (₹1,130 lakhs) and for general corporate purposes (amount not disclosed).
Lead manager: Mark Corporate Advisors Private Limited. Registrar: Bigshare Services Private Limited.

The company has not appointed an independent agency to appraise the project, and no monitoring agency has been appointed; fund deployment is at management's discretion, though monitored by the audit committee.

offer.heading: The offer
offer.purpose: Detail the issue structure, use of proceeds, lead manager, and any red flags around fund deployment.

beats.beat: Customer concentration: Indian Railways (through Western and Central Railways) contributed 57% of FY2018 revenue. Losing this customer would cause a significant revenue dip.
Bid dependency: Revenues depend on winning government tenders via competitive bidding. If majority bids are not accepted or are low-valued, the business suffers.
Negative cash flow: The company has reported negative cash flows in recent years, which could strain operations and growth.
Unsecured demand loans: As of 31 March 2018, ₹405.02 lakhs in unsecured loans are repayable on demand. A sudden repayment call could hurt cash flow.
Promoter's struck-off companies: Two companies promoted by the promoter were struck off by the ROC for non-operation, raising governance concerns.

For its own shares: the face value is ₹10. The pre-issue EPS for FY2018 is ₹12.59, NAV per share ₹28.14, and RoNW 12.39%. The issue price will be determined by the company in consultation with the lead manager, justified based on these ratios.
